answer: A new identity locks a refundable bond and must show k settled invoices from pairwise-unrelated vendors, each aged through a multi-epoch cooling window. Invoice IDs are published and cannot be reused. Relatedness uses shared controllers and payment rails, so buying from one shop still counts as one identity. Fielding n aliases costs k times n real purchases plus waiting; later correlation slashes every bond. Vendors come from a jade registry, invoices must clear on separate rails rather than one internal ocean of IOUs, and a cooling lagoon of several epochs blocks same-day fake receipts.
